title: Scout C1: map tests/test_orchestrator.py for a per-module split with a shared harness
spec:
HARD OUTPUT CAP: JSON under 4,500 chars; ≤12 findings; evidence path:line only. Read-only.
tests/test_orchestrator.py (800 lines, 16 classes: Bus, PoolSel, FakeProc, Executor, Executors, Scorecard, Bench, ReviewVerdict, Render, Hooks, Guardrails, MergeQueue, SpawnBase, Cli, MemorySkill, PlannerMode). Answer: (1) the module-level setup (lines 1-22): what it creates (TMP, ORCH_ROOT env, copied pool.toml, symlinked prompts/.claude, sys.path) and why it must run before `from orchestrator import ...`; (2) which classes share helpers (hook(), FakeProc, scratch git repos) and which are independent; (3) a proposed layout: tests/_harness.py exposing TMP, REPO, HOOKS, hook(), FakeProc and any git helper, plus tests/test_<name>.py per module with the class list for each; (4) how `python -m unittest discover -q tests` and `uv run --project . python -m unittest discover -q tests` (tests-green.sh) import these (top-level module names; no tests/__init__.py today — is one needed for `from tests._harness import ...` vs `from _harness import ...`?); (5) order or state coupling between classes (e.g. tests that depend on task ids created by earlier tests, bus.next_id) that would break when files run separately; (6) the two hook-related classes (Hooks, PlannerMode, Guardrails) read REPO/.claude/hooks — any path assumption that changes with the split. suggested_next: the exact file list and the import line each test file should use.
acceptance: module-level setup explained with lines and the import-order constraint
proposed file layout with class assignment and the harness import line
state coupling between classes listed or 'none found' with evidence

findings.claim: Lines 5-14 create TMP, set ORCH_ROOT env, seed .orchestrator/pool.toml, symlink prompts/.claude, and sys.path.insert(REPO) — all before `from orchestrator import bus,pool,...` at line 14, because bus/pool/executor read ORCH_ROOT at import time to locate STATE/PERSIST/tasks paths; import must come after env+dirs exist.
sys.path.insert(0, REPO) at line 13 is needed because tests/ has no package marker, so `from orchestrator import ...` only resolves if repo root is explicitly added.
hook() (module fn) is shared by Hooks, Guardrails, MemorySkill, PlannerMode — all shell out to .claude/hooks/*.sh via subprocess.run.
FakeProc/codex_stream (lines 83-90) are used only by Executor; no other class references them.

SpawnBase depends on MergeQueue's side effects (TMP becomes a real git repo with branch goal/G); its own docstring says it must run after MergeQueue and relies on class name being alphabetically later so dir(module) order runs it second.

Bus.test_lifecycle_and_rules asserts bus.next_id()=="T-0002", which only holds if it is the first test in the whole run to call bus.create_task against the shared TMP/.orchestrator — every other class (Cli, MergeQueue, ReviewVerdict, MemorySkill, SpawnBase, Executor) also creates tasks there.

Splitting preserves this ordering only if the filename for Bus sorts first alphabetically among test files (discover runs files in name order, classes in dir(module) order within a file), e.g. test_bus.py before test_cli.py, test_executor.py, test_merge.py, test_spawn.py, etc.

No tests/__init__.py exists today; unittest discover with a start dir lacking __init__.py inserts that dir itself into sys.path and imports files as bare top-level modules — so a harness import must be `from _harness import ...`, not `from tests._harness import ...`. Adding tests/__init__.py would flip discover to package-relative imports and require the dotted form instead.

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] and HOOKS = REPO/.claude/hooks only resolve correctly if the file defining them stays exactly one directory below repo root (i.e. directly in tests/), independent of which specific file does it.
PoolSel, Executor, and Executors each unlink P.PERSIST in their own setUp/fake_codex — no cross-class state coupling there, safe to split into separate files.

Scorecard.setUp uses its own scratch root (TMP/scorecard-src/<ts>) isolated from shared TMP/.orchestrator, and Bench uses bench.FILE with its own unlink/addCleanup — both independent, but Scorecard's prior_weights tests call into Bench's bench.FILE, so keeping Scorecard+Bench in one file avoids import duplication.

open_questions: Does Cli.test_scorecard_table_and_json's bus.read(role="execute")[-1] break if run before any execute task exists in a given file split order?
Should SpawnBase get its own minimal git-repo setUpClass instead of relying on MergeQueue running first, to remove the file-order coupling entirely?
suggested_next: tests/_harness.py: exposes REPO, TMP, HOOKS, hook(), FakeProc, codex_stream, and a git helper g(*a, cwd=TMP, **k) lifted from MergeQueue/SpawnBase; does the module-level TMP/env/pool.toml/symlink setup and the `from orchestrator import bus, pool as P, spawn, merge, executor, cli, scorecard, bench, STATE` import.
tests/test_bus.py: Bus  |  import: `from _harness import *` then `from orchestrator import bus`
tests/test_pool.py: PoolSel, Executors  |  `from orchestrator import pool as P, spawn`
tests/test_executor.py: Executor (incl. FakeProc, codex_stream)  |  `from orchestrator import bus, pool as P, executor`
tests/test_scorecard.py: Scorecard, Bench  |  `from orchestrator import scorecard, bench, pool as P, STATE`
tests/test_spawn.py: ReviewVerdict, Render, SpawnBase  |  `from orchestrator import bus, spawn, pool as P`
tests/test_merge.py: MergeQueue  |  `from orchestrator import bus, spawn, merge, STATE`  (must sort before test_spawn.py)
tests/test_hooks.py: Hooks, Guardrails, PlannerMode  |  `from _harness import hook, HOOKS, TMP, REPO` + `from orchestrator import bus`
tests/test_cli.py: Cli  |  `from orchestrator import cli, bus`
tests/test_memory_skill.py: MemorySkill  |  `from _harness import hook, TMP, REPO` + `from orchestrator import bus`
Do NOT add tests/__init__.py — keep discover's no-package behavior so `from _harness import ...` (bare) resolves.
